elements.evidence: The grant expressly covers “affiliated companies of Sparkling” operating at Authorized Locations.

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no licence right for contractors acting on Sparkling's behalf.
The clause does not make any paid-up licence perpetual, and it does not demonstrate that paid-up licences are inapplicable.
The clause does not make any paid-up licence irrevocable, and it does not demonstrate that paid-up licences are inapplicable.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated only for Customer's material breach.
elements.evidence: No restriction limits termination of a subscription licence to Sparkling's material breach, and subscription licensing is not demonstrably inapplicable.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated for material breach only if that breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: The clause supplies neither a cure right nor an uncured-breach termination trigger, and subscription licensing is not demonstrably inapplicable.

The added right is limited to a successor by merger or acquisition rather than successors generally. Section (d) also continues to require consent to assignment of Agreement rights, creating uncertainty as to the licence-transfer right.

elements.element: Licence extends to Customer's affiliates upon written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause grants affiliated companies use rights without requiring notice, which is broader than coverage upon written notice.

elements.element: Licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Although the grant says Sparkling may transfer the licence to a successor by merger or acquisition without approval and Section (c) is conformed, Section (d) still requires the other party's written consent to assignment of Agreement rights. The operative provisions therefore do not unambiguously permit the transfer without consent.

result.reason: The redline preserves and broadens the existing affiliate coverage and attempts the fallback M&A transfer right, but it fails to conform Section (d). That unresolved consent restriction conflicts with or materially clouds the new transfer right. It also omits contractor rights, perpetual and irrevocable paid-up rights, and subscription termination protections. The changes are narrowly directed to the requested fallback, but the internal conflict prevents either complete position from being achieved and means the drafting does not preserve coherent operative intent.
